task.title: Replace selected active tools atomically
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/635 by refreshing exact active tool adapters without discarding the working batch when changed artifacts fail validation.
acceptance_criteria: Preflight duplicate replacement IDs and require every exact ID to be active before mutation.
Prepare, compile, and construct the complete replacement selection before swapping adapters.
Preserve old and unrelated adapters on every staged or registry failure.
Keep guest execution deferred behind later caller-owned authorization and support explicit uniform limits.

attempts.summary: Established RED coverage for atomic active-adapter replacement.
attempts.diagnostic: Focused tests could not compile because the kernel replacement primitive, typed replacement errors, and extension replacement operations did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added kernel tests for deterministic batch preflight and extension tests for successful refresh, invalid artifacts, missing active IDs, empty selection, and old-adapter preservation.

attempts.diagnostic: Constructing the complete inert replacement batch before one preflighted registry commit avoids the downtime and partial state of sequential deactivation and activation.
attempts.patch: Added ToolRegistry::replace_all, ToolReplacementError, default and explicit-limit replacement operations, documentation, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Strengthened deferred-execution coverage during independent review.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial tests did not directly prove that a start-trapping guest stayed inert during replacement or that custom limits reached only a later invocation.
attempts.patch: Added focused tests for no guest instantiation during replacement and restrictive caller-selected limits during the subsequent authorized invocation.

outcome.summary: Selected active WebAssembly tools can now be refreshed atomically while invalid replacements leave the complete old batch invocable and invocation policy remains caller-owned.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test tool_registry batch_replacement
nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-extensions --test activation
GitHub Rust quality gate https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/actions/runs/30223655976 and substantive exact-head CodeRabbit review at https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/pull/636

lessons: Replacement should prove the new complete batch valid before discarding any working adapter.
Atomic registry preflight separates adapter construction failures from missing-active-ID failures cleanly.
A trapping component is useful evidence that lifecycle operations remain inert until invocation.
Duplicated activation and replacement pipelines should be consolidated in a bounded follow-up rather than expanded in the feature change.
